I have farmed these fields for 20 years. I never went to school. I learned everything by doing it and watching my father and the other farmers around here. I started with just a few mu, and every year I took more land from neighbors whose children went to work in the cities. Now I have almost 350 mu. That is too much for four people to work alone, so I hire tractors and hire workers when it is busy.

I grow maize, millet, and sweetpotato. Sweetpotato is my main crop. I have always grown these three. I do not try new things easily because if something fails on 350 mu, I lose everything.

For the maize, I plant hybrid seeds. Everyone uses hybrid now. I buy them by the bag from the seed dealer. Last year I put one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu at planting, and then I spread half a bag of urea when the plants were about knee-high. That gave me a good harvest. This year I will do the same. I hire the tractor man to do rotary tillage. I irrigate three times with my well — I pay workers to help move the pipes. I spray pesticide three times. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

For sweetpotato, I keep my own vines from last year. That saves money on seeds. Sweetpotato needs more potassium than the other crops. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, plus some extra potassium fertilizer — about one small bag for every two mu. I irrigate three times because the tubers need water when they are swelling. I spray pesticide three times. I expect about 2500 kg per mu.

For millet, I buy improved seeds from the market. Millet does not need as much. I put about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu. I irrigate twice because millet can handle dry weather. Pesticide twice. I expect about 250 kg per mu.

I watch what my neighbors do. Old Wang across the road has a similar farm. If he uses more fertilizer and gets better yield, I think about copying him. But this year I am doing what I did last year. On a farm this big, it is better to waste a little fertilizer than to risk a bad harvest. A bad harvest means I cannot pay the workers or the tractor man.
